tool_definitions.name: subagent
tool_definitions.description: start independent subagents with a shared optional system prompt and individual tasks, send a finished subagent a follow-up, and inspect or control them by name; at most 5 run at once; a subagent knows only a short description of its sandbox, your system_prompt, and its prompt: none of your instructions, context files or conversation reach it, so give it everything it needs; each subagent can read but not write its workspace, and has a shell only while you do, writing only to its own scratch, which you reach as subagents/<name> inside yours; finished subagents whose answers you have not read through output report back after a short batching window; you are woken by them if you have ended your turn, so end your turn rather than waiting or polling for them

parameters.name: names
parameters.description: the subagents for status, output, or stop; empty means all of them

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: the finished subagent to send a follow-up to (for send)

parameters.name: system_prompt
parameters.description: the only instructions every subagent shares, beside a short description of its sandbox (for start)

parameters.name: subagents

item_fields.name: prompt
item_fields.description: the whole task for this subagent, with whatever context it needs

item_fields.name: intent
item_fields.description: what this subagent is for, as a 5 to 7 word phrase opening with a capitalised -ing verb, such as "Reviewing the parser for missed errors"

item_fields.name: workspace
item_fields.description: the subagent's read-only workspace, any directory you can read; absent means yours

parameters.description: one task per independent subagent (for start)
